mutant.description: Every verdict in this cell is a STRING from the IAM policy simulator ('allowed' / 'implicitDeny') or a FINDING COUNT from accessanalyzer. Both read identically to an instrument looking at the wrong object: the cloud-ops profile records four independent false-deny modes for simulate-principal-policy, of which mode 3 (a typo'd action returns implicitDeny, indistinguishable from a missing grant) and mode 4 (a resource ARN at the wrong grain returns implicitDeny even for an admin principal) are the two that would make this cell's base FAIL meaningless. A zero-findings read from validate-policy has the same shape.
mutant.expected: validate-policy returning 0 findings on a live document must return INVALID_ACTION when a bogus action name is planted inside that same document. And the simulator's pre-act implicitDeny on a given ARN must be shown to be the WORLD rather than the grain, by the same call at the same grain for the same principal reading 'allowed' after the act.
mutant.observed: BOTH FIRED. (1) validate-policy reads findings=0 on each live after document; with s3:ZzzNoSuchActionName9999 planted into the first statement of the daily document, the same call returns INVALID_ACTION, rc=0 -- so the 0 is a real read and every one of the four added entries uses a real action name. (2) Mode 4 is EXCLUDED BY CONSTRUCTION, not by argument: the four calls that read implicitDeny before the apply are byte-identical in principal, action, resource ARN and context entries to the four that read 'allowed' after it, so a wrong-grain ARN cannot explain the base FAIL. The check also runs ONE --resource-arns per call (mode 1), passes --context-entries for the s3:prefix-conditioned ListBucket statement (mode 2), and runs its (d) positive control as a SEPARATE invocation, which is the only form in which a positive control is a control. (3) The (c) negative controls are live in BOTH directions: a security_names PUT and a sibling security_namesX GET read implicitDeny before AND after, so the widen is narrow and the instrument still says no when the answer is no.
